day_shape: 68 items: Trump floats another "little Epic Fury" strike on Iran, IRGC says two tankers hit mines south of Hormuz, Saudis intercept Houthi missile at Riyadh, Jerusalem Post reports Iran undersea-cable targeting plans, UNOCHA logs post-17 June MOU resurgence.

threads.label: Trump threats and renewed-strike debate
threads.summary: Trump said in Florida Washington may conduct another "little Epic Fury" operation against Iran, with Iran International reporting the US ambassador to the UN saying the naval blockade can be sustained for the "foreseeable future." Turkish FM Hakan Fidan warned renewed US or Israeli strikes would expand the regional war, and Istanbul diplomacy produced no breakthrough.

threads.label: Hormuz tankers and Gulf cable plans
threads.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers were hit by mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, and Jerusalem Post reported Iranian security officials have drawn up plans to target undersea internet cables in the Gulf if US or Israeli strikes resume. Defa Press carried General Abdollahi's claim Iran would not allow US warships to re-enter the Persian Gulf.

threads.label: Saudi/Yemen missile interception
threads.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a ballistic missile launched from Yemen towards Riyadh, with Iran International reporting Pakistani troops deployed to defend the kingdom against Tehran's allies while Islamabad mediates between Iran and the US. Defa Press framed Riyadh's Yemen policies as having empowered the Houthis.

threads.label: IDF Hebron operation and Gaza Yellow Line
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet launched a multi-day counterterrorism operation in Hebron following a Hamas shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers, with Netanyahu saying IDF soldiers prevented a wider civilian attack. The IDF separately said troops killed two people who crossed the Yellow Line in northern and southern Gaza.

threads.label: Iran domestic security posture
threads.summary: Iran International reported more visible armed patrols, checkpoints and degraded internet across Iran, while IRIB said two individuals linked to foreign intelligence services were arrested in Kermanshah. Jerusalem Post also reported US intelligence warnings of "advanced" Iranian assassination plots prompting evacuations.

threads.label: Regime political and religious messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message and audio reading for Hazrat Zaynab's birth and Nurses' Day, and the judiciary chief told Defa Press the "Zionist regime" is "dangerous for humanity." Pezeshkian visited the martyred leader's shrine and told officials people see "quarrels" instead of justice, while Defa Press warned of a "new round of Iran's regional war."

threads.label: Iran-Russia and UK political ties
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Iran's president will visit Russia next week for talks with Putin, as cited by the foreign minister. The Guardian, via Iran International, reported a billionaire Reform UK donor previously had a business venture with Astan Quds Razavi, the foundation under the Iranian supreme leader's authority.

The storm 'Cham­pi' is currently weakening and moving towards China's coasts.

events.title_en: Orange alert for intensity of rainfall system
events.summary_en: Orange alert for intensity of rainfall system. The Meteorological Organisation, forecasting intense activity of a rainfall system on Sunday, issued an orange alert for northern West Azerbaijan, East Azerbaijan and Ardabil, as well as the south and centre of Kerman. Severe downpours, hail and gusts of wind from this rainfall system could lead to flooding, slippery roads and damage to agricultural crops and temporary structures. It is recommended to avoid travelling in the riverbeds of these areas and necessary measures should be taken for harvesting agricultural and orchard crops in the affected areas.
